title: Comparative validation of multi-instance instrument segmentation in endoscopy: Results of the ROBUST-MIS 2019 challenge
shift: Natural procedure/domain gap; challenging blood/smoke/motion artifacts
method: Multi-team benchmark; increasing domain-gap validation stages
main: A canonical surgical robustness/generalization benchmark; performance worsens as domain gap increases.
limit: Primarily colorectal procedures from one institutional ecosystem; not a network/video-transport study.

title: Limited generalizability of single deep neural network for surgical instrument segmentation in different surgical environments
shift: Recording system; instrument morphology/version; surgery/procedure background
main: Generalization falls even under seemingly modest changes in camera system, instrument or procedure.
limit: Single study setting and task; factors are controlled but not a multicentre benchmark.

title: Challenges in multi-centric generalization: phase and step recognition in Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery
venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery 19:2249–2257
shift: Hospital/centre; workflow/technique; recording environment
main: Mono-centre models generalize poorly cross-centre; multicentre training improves generalization.
limit: Two centres and one procedure; centre shift bundles several causal factors.

title: Comparative validation of surgical phase recognition, instrument keypoint estimation, and instrument instance segmentation in endoscopy: Results of the PhaKIR 2024 challenge
task: Phase recognition; keypoints; instrument instance segmentation
shift: Medical centre / acquisition / workflow domain shift
main: Methods show poor cross-centre generalizability across all three evaluated tasks.
limit: Small number of full procedures; challenge-specific protocols.

title: Inter-hospital transferability of AI: A case study on phase recognition in cholecystectomy
shift: Hospital/surgeon/environment; manufacturer-specific instrument cues
dataset: 104 public surgeries from 3 centres + 21 local MHB videos
method: Public-only, local-only, combined and fine-tuned training
main: Public-only models transferred poorly to the local centre; diverse + site-specific data improved transfer.
limit: Task/procedure specific; local adaptation uses target-site data.

title: Optimizing latent graph representations of surgical scenes for unseen domain generalization
venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery 19:1243–1250
shift: Unseen centre; workflow/camera/patient variation
main: Object-centric scene representations are investigated to reduce unseen-centre domain sensitivity.
limit: Method-specific study; not a standardized corruption benchmark.

title: Overcoming color domain shift in endoscopic spine surgery: robust instrument segmentation via aggressive photometric augmentation
shift: Inter-institutional color/photometric shift
main: Baseline external DSC drops markedly; aggressive photometric augmentation restores strong external performance and reduces feature-domain discrepancy.
limit: Color shift is a specific factor; recent early-version article.

title: Benchmarking deep learning pipelines for surgical instrument segmentation in endoscopic spine surgery: cross-dataset evaluation under deployment-realistic conditions
shift: Temporal external + cross-dataset/institutional shift
dataset: SNUBH biportal (56 patients) + SEA uniportal (60 patients)
main: Cross-dataset performance can be detector-limited even for foundation-model pipelines; broader domain training substantially improves external results.
limit: Endoscopic-spine task; small external samples limit equivalence claims.

title: SegSTRONG-C: Segmenting Surgical Tools Robustly On Non-adversarial Generated Corruptions — An EndoVis'24 Challenge
shift: Photo-realistic smoke; over-bleeding; low brightness; digital corruptions
dataset: Mock endoscopic video sequences (6600 train / 3600 val / 5400 test cases on challenge site)
main: Direct surgical benchmark showing plausible non-adversarial corruptions materially challenge tool segmentation.
limit: Mock endoscopy rather than human surgery; current canonical report is preprint/challenge material.

title: CaRTS: Causality-Driven Robot Tool Segmentation from Vision and Kinematics Data
shift: Counterfactual low brightness, smoke, blood, altered background
main: Kinematics-informed causal segmentation preserves performance better than image-only baselines under counterfactual visual changes.
limit: Controlled dVRK setting; not human clinical deployment and not network telemetry.

title: Rethinking causality-driven robot tool segmentation with temporal constraints
venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery 18:1009–1016
shift: Unseen visual domains including smoke/blood; temporal robustness context
method: Temporal constraints + kinematics correction + spatio-temporal regularization
main: Temporal observability improves CaRTS convergence and maintains performance across tested domains.
limit: Not a controlled frame-loss/jitter study.

title: Simulation-to-real domain adaptation with teacher–student learning for endoscopic instrument segmentation
venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery 16:849–859
shift: Simulation-to-real; real-domain visual gap
method: Teacher–student UDA using labeled synthetic + unlabeled real data
main: Unlabeled real target frames improve sim-to-real segmentation over pure simulation training.
limit: UDA assumes access to target-domain unlabeled data.

title: Graph-Based Surgical Instrument Adaptive Segmentation via Domain-Common Knowledge
authors: Liu J, Guo X, Yuan Y
shift: Unlabeled target-domain shift
method: Interactive Graph Network; domain-common knowledge UDA
main: Representative surgical UDA work showing target-domain adaptation is already well established as a method family.
limit: Needs unlabeled target domain; not unseen-domain DG.

title: Generalizing Surgical Instruments Segmentation to Unseen Domains with One-to-Many Synthesis
shift: Unseen real domains / site-patient appearance variation
main: Synthetic data diversification can improve unseen-domain surgical instrument segmentation.
limit: Synthetic compositing does not reproduce every clinical shift mechanism.

title: SDA-CLIP: surgical visual domain adaptation using video and text labels
venue: Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery 13
shift: Virtual-reality/simulation to clinical domain
main: Video-text semantic alignment improves hard and soft cross-domain surgical action recognition.
limit: VR-to-clinical adaptation is not equivalent to hospital or communication shift.

title: Few-shot learning for surgical phase recognition: Performance and generalization in cholecystectomy
venue: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine 282:109386
shift: Cross-domain/domain-specific transfer with few-shot support
main: Performance declines as training domain moves farther from surgical target; domain-specific support remains important.
limit: Split definitions are study-specific and not a multicentre clinical benchmark.

title: Robustness evaluation of deep neural networks for endoscopic image analysis: Insights and strategies
shift: Clinically calibrated blur/exposure/color/compression/resolution distortions; compound corruption
dataset: Multiple endoscopy datasets + low-quality test set
main: Provides a strong severity-calibration and compound-corruption protocol precedent transferable as methodology, not surgical evidence.
limit: GI endoscopy cancer detection/diagnosis rather than surgical video.

title: On the Robustness of Temporal Vision-Language Models for Surgical Endoscopy Videos
shift: Defocus; haze; motion blur; shot noise; cautery smoke; packet-loss bursts
method: Endo-C6 fixed-high-severity controlled OOD benchmark + few-shot VeRA adaptation
main: Emerging direct evidence that packet-loss-like and visual corruptions can collapse temporal VLM performance.
limit: Very recent; fixed high severity; task is TVLM/video-text rather than conventional phase/segmentation.

title: Performance and Non-adversarial Robustness of the Segment Anything Model 2 in Surgical Video Segmentation
shift: Smoke; bleeding; low illumination on SegSTRONG-C
main: Foundation video segmentation is also evaluated under surgical non-adversarial corruptions; temporal prompting can affect robustness.
limit: Preprint; prompt-based zero-shot setting.

title: Reducing prediction volatility in the surgical workflow recognition of endoscopic pituitary surgery
venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery 17:1445–1452
shift: Temporal instability from occlusion/endoscope withdrawal (not a controlled network shift)
main: Temporal prediction instability is clinically relevant and can be reduced by smoothing.
limit: Does not manipulate frame loss, jitter or packet loss.

title: SurgflowNet: Leveraging unannotated video for consistent endoscopic pituitary surgery workflow recognition
shift: Temporal prediction consistency; limited-label setting
main: Consistency-focused training reduces unstable workflow predictions.
limit: Temporal consistency is not equivalent to communication-induced video corruption.

title: ROBUST-MIPS: A Combined Skeletal Pose and Instance Segmentation Dataset for Laparoscopic Surgical Instruments
shift: Inherits ROBUST-MIS procedure-domain structure
dataset: 10,040 ROBUST-MIS images with added pose labels
main: Extends the established robustness dataset to pose estimation and richer tool localization.
limit: Derived from ROBUST-MIS; not independent shift evidence.

title: Domain-agnostic weakly supervised surgical instrument segmentation
shift: Cross surgical domain and imaging modality
main: A domain-agnostic, weakly supervised foundation-model pipeline is evaluated across diverse surgical modalities.
limit: Different tasks/modalities complicate direct performance comparison; not a corruption benchmark.

title: RobustSurg: Tackling domain generalisation for out-of-distribution surgical scene segmentation
shift: Unseen centre / imaging modality / style-content variation
dataset: CholecSeg8k → newly curated HeiCholSeg; other OOD set
main: Shows active work specifically targeting surgical OOD scene segmentation from one source domain.
limit: Preprint; curated target dataset and claims require peer-reviewed confirmation.

title: CholecInstanceSeg: A Tool Instance Segmentation Dataset for Laparoscopic Surgery
shift: Observed hard cases: motion blur, smoke, blood/occlusion, reflections, lighting, lens dirtiness
method: Annotation protocol explicitly covers difficult visual conditions
main: Provides direct evidence that several proposed visual-shift factors occur in real laparoscopic data.
limit: Not itself a controlled robustness experiment.
